texts.preamble: Jagdish vs Rajesh on 15 January, 2026 In The Court Of Sh. Dev Saroha Civil Judge-04 (West) Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi Cnr no. Dlwt03-002681-2021 Cs Scj no. 1274/2021 Shri Jagdish, Son of Shri Udey Singh, R/o N-51, Gali no. 2, Vishnu Garden, New Delhi-110018. ........ Plaintiff Vs. 1. Shri Rajesh, Son of Sh. Jagdish. 2. Smt. Jamna, W/o Sh. Rajesh. Both R/o N-51, First Floor, Gali no. 2, Vishnu Garden, New Delhi-110018. ........ Defendants Date of institution of the suit : 21.10.2021 Date on which judgment was reserved : 15.01.2026 Date of pronouncement of Judgment : 15.01.2026 Suit For Mandatory Injunction And Permanent Injunction And For Recovery Of Damages/Mesne-Profits Judgment
texts.facts: 1. This is a suit for mandatory injunction, permanent injunction and for recovery of damages/mesne-profits filed on behalf of the plaintiff against the defendants. That, the plaintiff is an old aged person and is a peace loving and law abiding citizen and was residing at N-51, Gali no.2,Vishnu Garden, New Delhi-110018. 2.2. That, the plaintiff is the sole and absolute legal owner of the suit property by virtue of the legal title documents executed in favour of the plaintiff. That the said property is the self-acquired property of the plaintiff and therefore, the plaintiff is possessing all legal rights and title over the said property. The said property as legally owned by the plaintiff was built and purchased by him with his own funds and is comprised of total four floors i.e. ground, first, second and third floors. 2.3. That, the defendant no.1 is the son of the plaintiff and the defendant Jagdish vs Rajesh on 15 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30038978/ 1 no.2 is the wife of the defendant no.1. 2.4. That, the plaintiff being the legal owner of the said property had permitted the defendants to live and use the first floor of the said property temporarily, purely on license basis, without any monetary consideration. The remaining property is in the own use and occupation of the plaintiff and his family and the plaintiff has permitted his married daughter to live at third floor with her family and has also permitted his other son to live at second floor, and the plaintiff alongwith his wife has been living at ground floor of the said property. The said CS SCJ 1274/21 JAGDISH Vs. RAJESH Page no.2/32 property is more specifically shown in the site plan enclosed and the first floor, which is hereinafter referred to as the 'suit premises' is more specifically shown in red colour in the site plan annexed herewith. 2.5. That, however the behaviour of the defendants have always remained disrespectful and cruel towards the plaintiff, his wife and other family members and the defendants have always quarreled with the plaintiff and other family members and showed no regard or respect for them. 2.6. That, the defendants have ill motives and designs to somehow grab and usurp the said property of the plaintiff and the defendants particularly the defendant no.1 has already inflicted various physical assault and attempts on the life of the plaintiff and his other family members. The defendants have caused physical harm and injury to the plaintiff. 2.7. That, the defendants carried out physical assault on the daughter of the plaintiff namely Ms.Laxmi and she was taken to Guru Gobind Singh Hospital, Raghubir Nagar, by the police and MLC no. 65983/2020 dated 01.04.2020 was registered. The defendants also assaulted the wife of the plaintiff namely Kelam Devi and she was given medical treatment at the aforesaid hospital on 23.02.2021. CS SCJ 1274/21 JAGDISH Vs. RAJESH Page no.3/32 2.8. That, the defendants are unlawfully demanding money from the plaintiff for vacating and removing their unauthorized occupation over the suit property of the plaintiff. The plaintiff has made numerous complaints to the police authorities against the defendants. The plaintiff has given written complaint to the SHO,PS Khayala vide DD no. 18-A dated 04.08.2019. The plaintiff has also given complaint vide DD no. 27-B dated 27.10.2016 to the SHO, PS Khayala. 2.9. That, the defendants, along with family members & relations of the defendant no. 2, further carried out murderous assault and attempt on the life of the plaintiff, his wife, daughter and other family members on 25.07.2021 and because of the said assault with arms and weapons, the plaintiff, his wife, daughter and her child suffered grievous bodily injuries. The plaintiff was taken to Guru Gobind Singh Hospital, Raghubir Nagar, where MLC no.73199 dated 25.07.2021 was registered. 2.10. That, after committing the said murderous assault on the plaintiff and his family members, the defendants are creating hindrance and obstruction to the plaintiff, his wife and other family members to live at his own property and because of the said persisting threats by the defendants with other associates, the plaintiff alongwith his wife has been living in very terrible condition in a jhuggi in Rohini. CS SCJ 1274/21 JAGDISH Vs. RAJESH Page no.4/32 2.11. That, the defendants have been constantly extending threats to the plaintiff and his family to kill them by throwing 'acid' upon them. Jagdish vs Rajesh on 15 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30038978/ 2 The defendant no.1 has given the said threat on whatsapp number 9354513268 of the plaintiff from his mobile phone no.9999329336 and the plaintiff has also voice recording of the same. The plaintiff has given the written complaint to the SHO, PS Khayala and D.C.P. Janak Puri on 06.09.2021 against the defendants. 2.12. That, due to the said persisting quarrels, abuses and threats given by the defendants to the plaintiff, and other family members, the plaintiff and his family members are living under great fear and danger. The defendant no.2 has also threatened to commit suicide and involve the plaintiff and his family and already have made such attempts. 2.13. That, the plaintiff and his wife have severed all their relations with the defendants and have disowned and debarred the defendants. A public notice by the plaintiff and his wife of severing their relations with the defendants and disowning and disinheriting them from all their estate was published in daily newspaper "Jansatta" on 15th August, 2019. 2.14. That, the said legal notice was duly served upon the defendants, but the defendants have neither replied nor complied with the said legal notice and the defendants no.1 and 2 have failed to vacate and handover the possession of the suit premises to the plaintiff till date and hence, the present suit. 2.16. That, the plaintiff has again requested the defendants on 03.10.2021 to vacate and handover the possession of the suit premises, but instead the defendants refused and threatened the plaintiff and the defendants refused to vacate and handover the possession of the suit premises to the plaintiff and further threatened to handover the possession of the suit premises to some third person and not to the plaintiff at any cost. The defendants have further threatened to forcefully enter into the remaining property and dispossess the plaintiff from the whole of CS SCJ 1274/21 JAGDISH Vs. RAJESH Page no.6/32 the suit premises. 2.17 . That, the plaintiff is thus legally entitled to recover the possession of the suit premises from the defendants no.1 and 2 and the plaintiff is also entitled to the decree restraining the defendants from transferring and parting with possession of the suit premises to any third person as they have no right, title, or interest of any kind in the suit premises and further, from entering into any other portion of the property or causing any damage and loss to the suit premises and blocking entrance Jagdish vs Rajesh on 15 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30038978/ 3 and obstruction to the plaintiff with his family to live at his own property, etc. The plaintiff is also entitled to damages @ Rs.500/- per day from the defendants for unauthorized occupation of the suit premises from the date of filing of the suit. 2.18. That, the plaintiff has no other efficacious remedy except to file the present suit. The cause of action further arose when the defendants with others, inflicted physical injuries to the plaintiff and his family members. The cause of action further arose when the legal notice dated 14.09.2021 was served upon the defendants. The cause of action further arose on 03.10.2021 when the defendants threatened to part with possession of the suit premises and further to forcefully enter into the remaining property and forcefully dispossess the plaintiff from the property. The cause of action is still continuing as the defendants no.1 and 2 are in unauthorized use and occupation of the suit premises. 2.20. That, the parties to the suit reside and work for gain at Delhi, the cause of action has also arisen at Delhi and the suit premises is also situated within the territorial jurisdiction of this Hon'ble Court, hence, this Hon'ble Court has jurisdiction to try and entertain the present suit. That, the value of the suit for the purposes of court fee and jurisdiction is fixed at Rs.130/- each for the relief of permanent injunction and mandatory injunction over which the requisite court fee has been affixed. The plaintiff undertakes to pay the court fee for the damages at the time of passing of the decree. 2.22. It is, therefore, prayed that a decree of mandatory injunction be passed in favour of the plaintiff and against the defendants, thereby directing the defendants no.1 and 2 to remove their unauthorized occupation over the suit premises and vacate and handover the vacant, physical possession of the suit premises bearing no. N-51, First Floor, Gali No.2, Vishnu Garden, New Delhi-110018, more specifically shown red colour in the site plan and further, a decree of permanent injunction be passed in favour of the plaintiff and against the defendants, thereby restraining the defendants no.1 and 2 from transferring or parting with possession or creating any third party interest in the suit premises bearing no. N-51,First Floor, Gali No.2, Vishnu Garden, New Delhi-110018, as more specifically shown red colour in the site plan annexed and/or from causing any damage or loss to the suit premises, its structure, fittings, fixtures etc and that the defendants be further restrained from entering into any other portion of the said property and from locking/blocking/obstructing the plaintiff and his CS SCJ 1274/21 JAGDISH Vs. RAJESH Page no.9/32 family to live at his own property and from forcefully dispossessing the plaintiff from the remaining property. It is further prayed that a decree of mesne profits/ damages of Jagdish vs Rajesh on 15 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30038978/ 4 Rs.500/-(Rupees five hundred only) per day be also passed in favour of the plaintiff and against the defendants no.1 and 2 from the date of filing the suit till vacation of the suit premises for unauthorized use and occupation of the suit premises bearing no. N-51, first floor, Gali No.2, Vishnu Garden, New Delhi-110018, as more specifically shown red colour in the site plan annexed. 2.23. That the present suit is within the limitation period. 3. CASE OF DEFENDANTS AS SET UP IN WRITTEN STATEMENT 3.1. That, the suit of the plaintiff in its present form is not maintainable and hence, it is liable to be dismissed. 3.2. That, the suit has been filed by the plaintiff against the answering defendants without any cause of action and hence, the same is liable to be dismissed under order VII Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure. That, many times, the defendant no.2 was not allowed to take food by the plaintiff and many times, the defendant no.2 was turned out of the matrimonial house in three clothes alongwith the minor children. 5. In cross-examination dated 29.05.2024, this witness deposed that he is illiterate and that he does not understand English language. He further deposed that the affidavit had been prepared under his instructions in Hindi and the same was translated by his counsel in English. He deposed that he is residing in jhuggi at road in Rohini alongwith his wife. He admitted that he has one property in Bakkarwala, JJ Colony, House no, B-144, Delhi. He again deposed that the House number is B-143. He deposed that he purchased the above property from Sh.Chaman Lal and then again deposed that he purchased the said property from one Nathu Lal for an amount of Rs.2,25,000/- around 6-7 years back. He further deposed that he had got prepared the paper of the above said property from Nangloi, Delhi and he does not remember about the description of property paper. He denied the suggestion that he had taken forcible CS SCJ 1274/21 JAGDISH Vs. RAJESH Page no.16/32 possession of the above said property. He further deposed that he has not placed any property documents of the above said property in the present case. 7.4. He further deposed that he is the owner of N-51, Gali no.2, Vishnu Garden, Delhi and that he purchased the property in question from Sh.Omal about 25-26 years back for an amount of Rs. 3 lacs approximately. He further deposed that he got prepared the property paper of the property in question from District Center, Uttam Nagar, Delhi and that the property in question is measuring around 33 sq. yards. He further deposed that the property is constructed till four stories and that he is residing on the ground floor. He further deposed that in first floor defendant is residing and in second floor the daughter of plaintiff is residing and the third floor is on rent. 7.5. In his further cross-examination dated 13.02.2025, he deposed that today he had come to the Court from Rohini jhuggi and that he visits the suit property occasionally once or twice in a month as his another son and daughter are residing there on respective floors. He denied the suggestion that he had illegally grabbed the property and then voluntarily submitted that he purchased the same from his own funds. He further deposed that he is residing in the ground floor, his son Rajesh resides at first floor, another son Vinod resides at CS SCJ 1274/21 JAGDISH Vs. RAJESH Page no.17/32 second floor and his daughter Laxmi resides at third floor. He denied the suggestion that his daughter-in-law Ganga lodged a complaint against him in the police station. He deposed that there was no criminal case pending against him in past and present. He further deposed that he is not aware that some FIR no. 444/16, PS Khyala U/s 498-A/303-B/34 IPC was registered against him. In his cross-examination dated 09.12.2025, this witness admitted that legal notice dated 14.09.2021 exhibited as Ex.PW1/16 (colly.) through Counsel was sent by the plaintiff to him and the same was received by him. He further deposed that he does not know whether he had given any reply to the above stated legal notice. He admitted that his father lives on the ground floor of the suit property and his younger brother namely Vinod lives on the second floor of the suit property. He denied the suggestion his sister Laxmi lives on the third floor of the suit property and deposed that it is vacant. He further CS SCJ 1274/21 JAGDISH Vs. RAJESH Page no.22/32 deposed that no lock has been put on the third floor of the suit property by his father and stated that the doors are open. 8.4. This witness admitted that his father is the owner of the whole of the suit property and the documents of the whole of the suit property are in the name of his father. He admitted that he is in possession of the first floor of the suit property. 8.5. He further deposed that he cannot read and write English and can only read and write Hindi to a less extent and that he does not know what is written in his affidavit exhibited as Ex. DW1/A. He further deposed that he does not know where Ex. DW1/A was executed and on what date it was executed. He further deposed that he does not know whether his father has disowned him and his wife vide newspaper Ex. PW1/14 (OSR). He further deposed that he had filed police complaint Jagdish vs Rajesh on 15 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30038978/ 10 against his father for physical and mental violence and that he has not filed the same on record. He admitted that CS SCJ 1274/21 JAGDISH Vs. RAJESH Page no.23/32 in the FIR filed under section 498A/304B IPC against his father, his father was discharged.
texts.arguments: That, in the light of the aforesaid facts and circumstances, the plaintiff does not want to permit the defendants to stay, use and occupy the said first floor of CS SCJ 1274/21 JAGDISH Vs. RAJESH Page no.5/32 the suit premises, as a licensee any more and has therefore terminated and revoked the said license and permission granted to the defendants. That the plaintiff has served upon the defendants a legal notice dated 14 th September, 2021 and has called upon the defendants to vacate and handover the possession of the suit premises and remove their belongings and articles within 15 days of the receipt of the said legal notice, otherwise, they will be liable to pay Rs.500/- per day as damages/mesne profits. 2.15. The defendants have also interfered and stopped the plaintiff and his wife to live in his own property and the plaintiff alongwith his wife is forced to live in a jhuggi. 2.19. That, the cause of action for filing the present suit arose in favour of the plaintiff and against the defendants, firstly when at the request of the defendants no.1 and 2, the plaintiff permitted the defendants no.1 and 2 to use the suit premises temporarily as they assured to arrange their own accommodation and shift therein and vacate CS SCJ 1274/21 JAGDISH Vs. RAJESH Page no.7/32 and handover the possession of the suit premises to the plaintiff. The cause of action also arose on various dates and occasions when the defendants harassed, threatened and humiliated the plaintiff and made the life of the plaintiff and his family a hell. That the cause of action further arose when the defendant no.2 alongwith her family members created hindrance and obstruction to the plaintiff and her family members. 3.8. That the plaintiff has been giving the false information in the present case only to mislead the Hon'ble Court as in para no.1 of the plaint, the plaintiff has alleged that he CS SCJ 1274/21 JAGDISH Vs. RAJESH Page no.12/32 is residing in Jhuggi in Rohini, Delhi, however, on the documents filed with the suit at Serial no. 61, he has submitted that he is living below Tagore Garden Metro Station. He denied the suggestion that he was declared a proclaimed offender in the above case. He further deposed that it was a false and fabricated criminal case against him and he had been acquitted in that matter. He denied the suggestion that he was detained in judicial custody in that matter for a period of 3 months. He then voluntarily deposed that he was in judicial custody for about 15 days only. He denied that the defendant in the present matter was the person who stood as surety in the said criminal matter at the time of grant of bail. He denied that NCR no. 0084/2021, PS Khyala was lodged against him for beating the wife of his son Vinod. He denied that he had filed the present suit with malafide intention and ulterior motive so that his son/defendant no.1 namely Rajesh divorce his wife i.e defendant no. 2 namely Jamuna in the present matter. He denied the suggestion that he had ever beaten the defendant no.2 for dowry. He admitted that he had lodged a complaint Ex.PW-1/12 before SHO, PS Khyala, CS SCJ 1274/21 JAGDISH Vs. RAJESH Page no.18/32 on the ground that his sons are trying to dispossess him from the suit property. He admitted that in the said complaint he had mentioned that defendant no.1 and 2 had ousted him Jagdish vs Rajesh on 15 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30038978/ 8 from the suit property on 25.09.2021. 7.6. On being questioned whether it is correct that the complaint Ex.PW-1/12 is dated 06.09.2021, the Court recorded an observation that the witness is not responding to this question and is further challenging that Ex.PW-1/12 i.e. the complaint was not made by him. He denied the suggestion that he had made false and fabricated complaints against the defendant in the concerned PS. 7.7. He further denied the suggestion that he inflicted the above said injuries to himself to falsely implicate the defendants. He denied that he was merely treated for fever and vomiting. He denied suggestion that no complaint was made by him against his father. 8.6. He further deposed that he does not know whether his maternal grandmother had given any money to his father for his kids and that he does not know why this has been mentioned in para no. 6 of his affidavit. He denied the suggestion that NCR marked as Mark-C was registered on the basis of false complaint. 9.4. The case of the plaintiff in brief is that the plaintiff is the sole and absolute legal owner of the property bearing no.N-51, Vishnu Garden, New Delhi-110018 measuring 33.1/4 sq yds by virtue of the legal title documents executed in favour of the plaintiff which are exhibited as Ex. PW1/3 (OSR) (colly.). It is submitted that plaintiff lives on the ground floor of the above said property, his another son namely Vinod lives on the second floor of the above said property and his daughter namely Laxmi lives on the third floor of the abovesaid property. It is further submitted on behalf of the plaintiff that the defendants are intending to sell the suit premises to third persons and are not only threatening the plaintiff and his family members but are also interfering in the portion of the abovesaid property where plaintiff and his family members reside. The plaintiff has also relied upon documents i.e Ex.PW-1/1(OSR) which is copy of Aadhaar Card, Ex.PW-1/2 which is site plan, Ex.PW-1/4(OSR) which is MLC no.65983/2020, Ex.PW-1/5(OSR) which is copy of written complaint to SHO, PS Khyala dated 04.08.2019, Ex.PW-1/6(OSR) which is copy of complaint dated 27.10.2016 to SHO PS Khyala, Ex.PW-1/7 (OSR) which is emergency card of plaintiff of Guru Gobind Singh Govt. Hospital, Ex.PW-1/9 (OSR) (colly) which is copy of MLC and emergency card of plaintiff's wife Mrs. Kelam and daughter Lakshmi dated 25.07.2021, Ex.PW-1/10 (colly) which are photographs of assault showing injuries upon plaintiff, his wife and daughter, Ex. RAJESH Page no.27/32 Legal notice dated 14.09.2021 alongwith postal receipts in support of his case. 9.7. Per contra, on behalf of the defendants, it is argued that the plaintiff has filed false and frivolous case against them. It is submitted on behalf of the defendants that plaintiff is himself a person of disputable character and that all the allegations made by the plaintiff are false. It is further submitted that the grandmother in law of defendant no. 2 sold her property before her death and had given Rs. 28,00,000/- to each of her grandson i.e Vinod and Rajesh (defendant no.1), who were minor at that time and the plaintiff had misused that amount in purchasing the properties at B-144 and A-414, Bakkarwala, J.J. Colony, Delhi and at some other places in the name of his wife. It is submitted that when Vinod and Rajesh demanded their shares from their father i.e plaintiff , the plaintiff started giving them threats. It is further submitted that the plaintiff has made a false submission that he is living below Tagore Garden Metro Station. Further, as already CS SCJ 1274/21 JAGDISH Vs. RAJESH Page no.29/32 stated, Ex. PW1/3 (OSR) (colly.) and Ex. PW1/15 shows that he has a better title to the above stated property then the defendants, though, on the basis of the above stated documents, he cannot be said to be the owner of the above stated property in the legal sense of the term, but still he has a better title than the defendants.

He admitted that in the said complaint he had mentioned that defendant no.1 and 2 had ousted him Jagdish vs Rajesh on 15 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30038978/ 8 from the suit property on 25.09.2021. 7.6. On being questioned whether it is correct that the complaint Ex.PW-1/12 is dated 06.09.2021, the Court recorded an observation that the witness is not responding to this question and is further challenging that Ex.PW-1/12 i.e. the complaint was not made by him. He denied the suggestion that he had made false and fabricated complaints against the defendant in the concerned PS. 7.7. He further denied the suggestion that he inflicted the above said injuries to himself to falsely implicate the defendants. He denied that he was merely treated for fever and vomiting. He denied suggestion that no complaint was made by him against his father. 8.6. He further deposed that he does not know whether his maternal grandmother had given any money to his father for his kids and that he does not know why this has been mentioned in para no. 6 of his affidavit. He denied the suggestion that NCR marked as Mark-C was registered on the basis of false complaint. 9.7. Per contra, on behalf of the defendants, it is argued that the plaintiff has filed false and frivolous case against them. It is submitted on behalf of the defendants that plaintiff is himself a person of disputable character and that all the allegations made by the plaintiff are false. It is further submitted that the grandmother in law of defendant no. 2 sold her property before her death and had given Rs. 28,00,000/- to each of her grandson i.e Vinod and Rajesh (defendant no.1), who were minor at that time and the plaintiff had misused that amount in purchasing the properties at B-144 and A-414, Bakkarwala, J.J. Colony, Delhi and at some other places in the name of his wife. It is submitted that when Vinod and Rajesh demanded their shares from their father i.e plaintiff , the plaintiff started giving them threats. It is further submitted that the plaintiff has made a false submission that he is living below Tagore Garden Metro Station.
